arxiv-2211-05608.title: Finitary simulation of infinitary β-reduction via Taylor expansion, and applications
arxiv-2211-05608.creator: Rémy Cerda ORCID:0000-0003-0731-6211, Lionel Vaux Auclair ORCID:0000-0001-9466-418X
arxiv-2211-05608.description: Abstract . Originating in Girard’s Linear logic, Ehrhard and Regnier’s Taylor expansion of λ-terms has been broadly used as a tool to approximate the terms of several variants of the λ-calculus. Many results arise from a Commutation theorem relating the normal form of the Taylor expansion of a term to its Böhm tree.

arxiv-2304-00190.title: Enormous variation in homogeneity and other anomalous features of room temperature superconductor samples: a Comment on Nature 615, 244 (2023)
arxiv-2304-00190.creator: J. E. Hirsch
arxiv-2304-00190.description: Abstract The resistive transition width of a recently discovered room temperature near-ambient-pressure hydride superconductor roomtlh changes by more than three orders of magnitude between different samples, with the transition temperature nearly unchanged. For the narrowest transitions, the transition width relative to T c T_{c} is only 0.014 % 0.014\% .

arxiv-2408-11821.title: MIMA 2.0 - Compact and Portable Multifunctional IoT integrated Menstrual Aid
arxiv-2408-11821.creator: Jyothish Kumar J, Subhankar Mishra, Shreya Shivangi, Amish Bibhu, Sulagna Saha
arxiv-2408-11821.description: Abstract The shredding intrauterine lining or the endometrium is known as Menstruation. It occurs every month and causes several issues like Menstrual Cramps and ache s in the abdominal region, stains, menstrual malodor, rashes in intimate areas , and many more. In our research, almost all of the products available in the market do not cater to these problems single-handedly.

arxiv-2410-06765.title: To Preserve or To Compress: An In-Depth Study of Connector Selection in Multimodal Large Language Models
arxiv-2410-06765.creator: Junyan Lin, Haoran Chen, Dawei Zhu, Xiaoyu Shen
arxiv-2410-06765.description: Abstract In recent years, multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have garnered significant attention from both industry and academia. However, there is still considerable debate on constructing MLLM architectures, particularly regarding the selection of appropriate connectors for perception tasks of varying granularities. This paper systematically investigates the impact of connectors on MLLM performance.

arxiv-2411-09831.title: 11 B states above the α \alpha -decay threshold studied via 10 B ( d , p ) 11 (d,p){}^{11} B
arxiv-2411-09831.creator: A. N. Kuchera, G. Ryan, G. Selby, D. Snider, S. Anderson, S. Almaraz-Calderon, L. T. Baby, B. A. Brown, K. Hanselman, E. Lopez-Saavedra, K. T. Macon, G. W. McCann, K. W. Kemper, M. Spieker, I. Wiedenhöver

Fox Superconducting Linear Accelerator Laboratory.

arxiv-2506-13756.title: UltraZoom: Generating Gigapixel Images from Regular Photos
arxiv-2506-13756.creator: Jingwei Ma, Vivek Jayaram, Brian Curless, Ira Kemelmacher-Shlizerman, Steven M. Seitz
arxiv-2506-13756.description: Abstract . We present UltraZoom, a system for generating gigapixel-resolution images of objects from casually captured inputs, such as handheld phone photos. Given a full-shot image (global, low-detail) and one or more close-ups (local, high-detail), UltraZoom upscales the full image to match the fine detail and scale of the close-up examples.

arxiv-2511-11031.title: Accelerating Controllable Generation via Hybrid-grained Cache
arxiv-2511-11031.creator: Lin Liu, Huixia Ben, Shuo Wang, Jinda Lu, Junxiang Qiu, Shengeng Tang, Yanbin Hao
arxiv-2511-11031.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Lin Liu, Huixia Ben, Shuo Wang, Jinda Lu, Junxiang Qiu, Shengeng Tang, Yanbin Hao. Controllable generative models have been widely used to improve the realism of synthetic visual content. However, such models must handle control conditions and content generation computational requirements, resulting in generally low generation efficiency. To address this issue, we propose a H ybrid- G rained C ache ( HGC ) approach that reduces computational overhead by adopting cache strategies with different granularities at different computational stages.

pmc-11289351.title: Targeting sphingolipid metabolism in chronic lymphocytic leukemia
pmc-11289351.creator: Flora Nguyen Van Long, Trang Le, Patrick Caron, Délya Valcourt-Gendron, Roxanne Sergerie, Isabelle Laverdière, Katrina Vanura, Chantal Guillemette
pmc-11289351.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Elevated levels of circulating C16:0 glucosylceramides (GluCer) and increased mRNA expression of UDP-glucose ceramide glycosyltransferase (UGCG), the enzyme responsible for converting ceramides (Cer) to GluCer, represent unfavorable prognostic markers in chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) patients.

pmc-11442297.title: Extrachromosomal circular DNAs in prostate adenocarcinoma: global characterizations and a novel prediction model
pmc-11442297.creator: Qingliu He, Qingfu Su, Chengcheng Wei, Pu Zhang, Weihui Liu, Junyi Chen, Xiaoping Su, Wei Zhuang
pmc-11442297.description: BackgroundThe role of focal amplifications and extrachromosomal circular DNA (eccDNA) is still uncertain in prostate adenocarcinoma (PRAD). Here, we first mapped the global characterizations of eccDNA and then investigate the characterization of eccDNA-amplified key differentially expressed encoded genes (eKDEGs) in the progression, immune response and immunotherapy of PRAD.

pmc-11454849.title: 12525 Feline Hypersomatotropism In The USA And Canada: Demographics Of 4620 Cats With Presumed Acromegaly
pmc-11454849.creator: Rebecca J Egbert, Robert C Fowkes, Stijn J M Niessen, Brian K Petroff
pmc-11454849.description: Disclosure: R.J. Egbert: None. R.C. Fowkes: None. S.J. Niessen: None. B.K. Petroff: None.Spontaneous models of endocrinopathies are powerful tools to understand disease etiology. Endocrine diseases in companion animals are particularly useful to study, as they share their environment with humans and typically present with clinical disease that phenocopies human symptoms.

pmc-11565103.title: Identifying a CD8T cell signature in the tumor microenvironment to forecast gastric cancer outcomes from sequencing data
pmc-11565103.creator: Xiangyue Zeng, Tiannake Shapaer, Jianguo Tian, Abulajiang Abudoukelimu, Zeliang Zhao, Paerhati Shayimu, Binlin Ma
pmc-11565103.description: BackgroundThe tumor microenvironment (TME) could be critical in carcinogenesis, immune evasion, and treatment response. TME-related genes are limited in their ability to predict gastric cancer (GC) outcomes. We utilized data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) to investigate the functional roles of TME-related genes in GC.

pmc-11602879.title: Serous endometrial carcinoma metastatic to the sigmoid colon masquerading as a primary colon cancer detected by bowel obstruction
pmc-11602879.creator: Taiga Shimura, Naoko Fukushima, Kazuto Tsuboi, Toshimasa Suzuki, Tetsuya Kajimoto
pmc-11602879.description: BackgroundThe majority of colorectal malignancies are primary tumors. Secondary tumors are rare, and colorectal metastasis from endometrial carcinoma is exceptionally uncommon. We report a case of serous endometrial carcinoma that metastasized to the sigmoid colon, initially presenting as a primary colon carcinoma due to bowel obstruction.Case presentationA 79-year-old woman presented with abdominal distention and constipation.

pmc-12379969.title: Triplet-to-singlet FRET (TS-FRET) in pure organic phosphors: emerging applications and new opportunities
pmc-12379969.creator: Sundaravalli Narayanan, Anju Ajayan Kongasseri, Subi J. George
pmc-12379969.description: Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) involving spin conversion from the triplet to the singlet state, commonly referred to as triplet-to-singlet FRET (TS-FRET) or phosphorescence energy transfer, has recently emerged as an active area of research in purely organic systems, driven by the development of efficient organic phosphors.

pmc-12401530.title: Beyond Mean Absolute Relative Difference (MARD): Rethinking Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) Evaluation for Real-World Diabetes Care
pmc-12401530.creator: Matteo Acanfora, Erika Pedone, Barbara Presciuttini, Francesca Ré, Luca Acanfora
pmc-12401530.description: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has transformed diabetes mellitus management, evolving from a supportive monitoring tool to a central pillar of care. For people with type 1 diabetes and many insulin-treated individuals with type 2 diabetes, CGM now directly informs treatment decisions, especially when integrated with automated insulin delivery (AID) systems.

pmc-13316798.title: The Oral–Endocrine Interface: Clinical Oral Health Burden, Oral Health‐Related Quality of Life, and Psychosocial Determinants in Women With Polycystic Ovary Syndrome—Evidence for Cross‐Disciplinary Prevention
pmc-13316798.creator: Jeevan V. Sambasivan, Deepak Kumar Singhal, Nishu Singla, Jishnu Pradeep, Aadil Abdulhameed
pmc-13316798.description: BackgroundThis study compared oral health status and oral health‐related quality of life (OHRQoL) in women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and age‐matched healthy controls and identified psychosocial and lifestyle determinants of oral health outcomes.Materials and MethodsA cross‐sectional study enrolled 72 women aged 18–45 years (36 PCOS, 36 controls) from a gynecology outpatient department, with PCOS confirmed using 2003 Rotterdam criteria.

pmc-13445830.title: Implementing AI-enabled chest X-ray for community-based integrated screening for tuberculosis, chronic respiratory diseases, and cardiovascular diseases in Nigeria
pmc-13445830.creator: Chidimma Okoye, Jude Ilozumba, John Oko, Amana Effiong, Young Oluokun, Chinwe Eze, Obioma Akaniro, Emperor Ubochioma, Collins Nwachi Ugwu, Rena Fukunaga, Toufiq Rahman, John Bimba, Jacob Creswell, Chukwuebuka Ugwu
pmc-13445830.description: BackgroundLow- and middle-income countries face a growing dual burden of communicable and non-communicable diseases, while services remain vertically organised. In Nigeria, tuberculosis (TB) services are established at primary care level, whereas access to cardiovascular disease (CVD) and chronic respiratory disease (CRD) care remains limited in rural settings.

pmc-13479415.title: Nutritional knowledge, sustainable food practices and food safety, in child and youth care facilities in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa
pmc-13479415.creator: Mumsy Evidence Chibe, Carin Napier, Heleen Grobbelaar
pmc-13479415.description: BackgroundChild and Youth Care Centres (CYCCs) play an important role in providing nutritional support to disadvantaged children and youth. However, little is known about how food handlers apply national nutrition and food hygiene standards in resource-constrained CYCC settings in South Africa.
